title: Brace a sagging gate so it holds itself up
instruction: The garden gate has sagged: its latch side has dropped onto the rubber stop. Fit the loose wooden brace between two of the corner seats so that the gate holds itself up, with the top of the latch-side stile no more than 3 mm from level with the top of the hinge-side stile, then let go of the gate and the brace.
context: Hanging and bracing gates is fence and carpentry work (O*NET 47-4031.00, Fence Erectors). A gate brace must run from the bottom of the hinge side to the top of the latch side so the gate's weight puts it in compression (Jacksons Fencing, "Which way should a garden gate be braced"). Both seat pairs accept the loose brace: the wrong diagonal is easier to fit and does nothing; the right one goes in only after the latch side is lifted square.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). A tabletop model of a garden gate (about 1:5 scale), standing upright across the table with its face towards the robots: two stiles (green-painted pine, 15 x 20 x 150 mm, 15 mm front to back) and two rails (green-painted pine, 15 x 20 x 220 mm), joined at each corner by a pivot pin running front to back. The pins are 200 mm apart along the rails (at y +10.5 and y -9.5) and at 45 mm and 165 mm above the table, all in the plane x 33. The hinge-side (left, +y) stile is fixed to a wooden post (20 x 20 x 200 mm, standing on the table and screwed to it, with its centre 20 mm behind and 20 mm to the left of the stile's centre line, at x 35, y +12.5) so it stays plumb, its bottom 30 mm above the table. The latch-side (right) stile carries an 80 g weight on its back face (20 x 40 x 20 mm overall: a 12.5 mm thick steel block on a 7.5 mm pine spacer; centred 105 mm above the table when square) and a 12 x 60 x 12 mm wooden handle sticking out to the right from its outer face, 100 mm above the table (when square). It has sagged: its bottom rests on a black rubber stop block (30 x 30 x 16 mm, glued to the table; it must not be moved) under it, 14 mm lower than when the frame is square, and the rails slope down to the right. Seats: in each of the frame's four inside corners, a V notch made of two pine plates (35 x 22 x 3 mm, at 90 degrees, opening along the diagonal towards the opposite corner) with a 2 x 26.4 x 26.4 mm pine back plate against the frame's face, standing 35 mm out from the frame's front face (towards the robots) and fixed to the rail it sits on. Brace: a pine dowel 12 mm across with a 15 mm ball on each end, 183.9 mm between the balls' centres (198.9 mm overall), 30 g (a 4 mm steel rod runs through its core and both balls), lying on the table along y (left-right) with its centre at x 20, y 0. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured at the end with a steel rule and a photo. 0 unless the brace sits in two diagonally opposite seats (each ball end resting in its notch, its centre within 3 mm of where it would touch both faces of the V, and no more than 28 mm out from where it would touch the seat's back plate), no part of either robot is within 20 mm of any part of the gate (frame, seats, weight, handle, post), the stop or the brace, and the gate is at rest (in the real world, measured 5 s after the robot lets go; in simulation, the latch side moved no more than 0.2 mm over the last second). Then by how far the top of the latch-side stile sits from level with the top of the hinge-side stile: within 3 mm 1.0; within 6 mm 0.5; within 9 mm 0.2; further 0. The trial ends early once the score has been 1.0 for 1 s.
reset_notes: Take the brace out of the seats and lay it back on the table along y, centred at x 20, y 0. The gate drops back onto its stop by itself. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: All rigid. The gate is a pin-jointed parallelogram (light damping, no pin friction); the hinge-side stile is fixed, as if hung on a plumb post. Its corners resist no racking, so the brace alone holds it; the 80 g weight stands in for a real gate's weight. The brace is a loose push-fit member in V-notch seats, not cut and nailed: it carries load the same way, in compression, and cannot pull. It is the square seat-to-seat length less 0.8 mm. Friction 0.6 (gate, brace) and 0.9 (rubber stop).
